title: Scale the portions, not the pan
hook: A four-portion recipe uses 300g. How much corresponds to six portions?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Scale a recipe quantity while preserving quantity per portion.

misconception: The same ingredient quantity serves more people without changing portion size.
objective: Scale a recipe quantity while preserving quantity per portion.

claims.text: The quantity-only recipe uses 300g for four equal portions. Scaled model; quantities only.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. FC LH-2 (2026-10-14, fresh fact-checker instance, W-369): verified: matches the scenario in the rendered question and the assumptions line "Full scale:900g; quantities only." (75×12 = 900 = resourceGraphicScale).

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Portions=6, A=450g and B=300g. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",75,"x"]; B=300; x denotes Portions. At x=6, A=450, B=300; Transfer recall: A at x=10 gives 750g (300÷4×10). Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The original rate is 75g per portion. Multiply that rate by the new portion count to keep the same amount per person. This demonstrates proportional quantity arithmetic, not cooking or nutritional advice.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",75,"x"]; B=300; x denotes Portions. At x=6, A=450, B=300; Transfer recall: A at x=10 gives 750g (300÷4×10). Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: A quantity-only recipe uses 300g for four equal portions. How many grams keep the same amount per portion for two portions? Correct: 150g. The rate is 75g per portion; two portions × 75g = 150g. This is proportional quantity arithmetic only.
claims.source: Quantity-only arithmetic: 300g ÷ 4 portions = 75g/portion; 75g/portion × 2 portions = 150g (the current recall; W-383 replaced the stale ten-portion, 750g note on 2026-10-14). The recall asks for proportional quantity, not the unchanged comparison. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/recall-patch-resources.lines.txt), applied 2026-10-14 by demo-builder; c4 restates the new recall item. FC LH-2 (2026-10-14, fresh fact-checker instance, W-369): verified: 300 g ÷ 4 = 75 g; 75 × 2 = 150 g (keyed option 0); stage at Portions=2 shows (75×2) = 150g.

claims.text: Cooking times do not scale in proportion to quantity: follow the recipe's own times and check food is cooked through.
claims.source: Safety-required stage line; wording from the independent safety second reader (company/reviews/lh-scale-recipe-portions/2026-10-14-safety.md, lifehacks-safety-reviewer), applied 2026-10-14 by demo-builder (W-373). Source owed: a food-safety body guidance, to be found and checked by the fact-checker. The reviewer named none, and none is asserted here. FC LH-2 (2026-10-14, fresh fact-checker instance, W-369): held unverified: an advice claim that needs a food-safety body (e.g. USDA FSIS, UK FSA); none could be opened from this host (proxy 403, DNS fail). Not verified on an unopened source. My read of the wording: accurate as now written (times change with quantity, not in proportion).
